On the (in)validity of the NLS-KdV system in the study of water waves 00footnotetext: 2010 AMS Subject Classification: 35Q31, 35Q35, 35Q53, 35Q55. 00footnotetext: Key words: Euler equations, linear Schrödinger equation, NLS equation, KdV equation, NLS-KdV system. 00footnotetext: Corresponding author: nghiem.nguyen@usu.edu.

CHUANGYE LIU
School of Mathematics and Statistics and Hubei Key Laboratory of Mathematical Sciences,
Central China Normal University, Luo-Yu Road 152, Wuhan, 430079, P.R. China
NGHIEM V.NGUYEN
Department of Mathematics and Statistics,
Utah State University, Logan, UT 84322-3900, USA
Abstract

It is universally accepted that the cubic, nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) models the dynamics of narrow-bandwidth wave packets consisting of short dispersive waves, while the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) models the propagation of long waves in dispersive media. A system that couples the two equations seems attractive to model the interaction of long and short waves and such a system has been studied over the last few decades. However, questions about the validity of the system in the study of water waves were raised in our previous work where we presented our analysis using the fifth-order KdV as the starting point. In this paper, these questions are settled unequivocally as we show that the NLS-KdV system or even the linear Schrödinger-KdV system cannot be resulted from the full Euler equations formulated in the study of water waves.

1 Introduction

For the last few decades, considerable attention (e.g. [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8]) has been devoted to the study of the following system, which has been termed the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger-Korteweg-deVries (NLS-KdV) system:

(1.1) {i​ut+ux​x+a​|u|2​u=−b​u​v,vt+c​v​vx+vx​x​x=−b2​(|u|2)x,\left\{\begin{matrix}\begin{split}iu_{t}+u_{xx}+a|u|^{2}u&=-buv,\\ v_{t}+cvv_{x}+v_{xxx}&=-\frac{b}{2}(|u|^{2})_{x},\end{split}\end{matrix}\right.

where x,t∈ℝx,t\in\mathbb{R}, v⁡(x,t)v(x,t) is a real-valued function, u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) is complex-valued and a,b,ca,b,c are real constants. In the context of water waves, the NLS-KdV system was originally introduced by Kawahara et al. [12] in the form

(1.2) {i⁡(∂u∂t2+k​∂u∂x2)+p​∂2u∂x12=q​u​v,∂v∂t3+∂v∂x3+32​v​∂v∂x1+r​∂3v∂x13=−s​∂|u|2∂x1,\left\{\begin{matrix}\begin{split}i\bigg(\frac{\partial u}{\partial t_{2}}+k\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_{2}}\bigg)+p\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}&=quv,\\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial t_{3}}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial x_{3}}+\frac{3}{2}v\frac{\partial v}{\partial x_{1}}+r\frac{\partial^{3}v}{\partial x_{1}^{3}}&=-s\frac{\partial|u|^{2}}{\partial x_{1}},\end{split}\end{matrix}\right.

where k,p,q,rk,p,q,r and ss are real constants, xn=ϵn​xx_{n}=\epsilon^{n}x, tn=ϵn​tt_{n}=\epsilon^{n}t. Here ϵ\epsilon is the small parameter in terms of which the asymptotic expansions were performed. This system couples two of the most studied equations in mathematical physics: the KdV equation describes the unidirectional propagation of long, nonlinear dispersive waves, while the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation governs the slowly varying modulation of a narrow bandwidth train of short waves. Both equations possess important features such as being completely integrable, exhibiting solitary-wave solutions, to name a few [10, 14]. As such, the system (1.2) is interesting from both mathematical and physical point of view.

However, there are several concerns regarding the above system which have been ignored thus far. Even though many authors (the papers [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8] are but a small sample of the relevant literature) have studied different mathematical aspects of system (1.1), there exists a tendency to cross reference without checking the details of the original derivation. Tracing through a plethora of references, the exact derivation of system (1.1) is nowhere to be found. We were led eventually to the paper by Kawahara et al. [12] which appears to be where the system (1.2) was first introduced in the context of water waves. Notice that the first equation in (1.2) is linear whilst that in (1.1) is nonlinear. Further, the time scales appearing in (1.2) are inconsistent, with the dynamics of the second equation of (1.2) appearing on a slower time scale than that of the first equation. More on this is discussed below. The same is true for the derivation in the context of plasma physics, see [4, 11, 13], where references lead back to [15] and the system (1.1) is not found in any form. Thus it appears that works heretofore studying (1.1) are investigating the mathematical aspects of a hypothetical system that has never been derived consistently. Of course, these mathematical considerations are perfectly valid in their own right, but it should be stated that to this point, the results presented are yet to be shown relevant in the context of any application. Many authors refer to one or multiple of [9, 11, 12, 13] and each other to motivate the use of the system (1.1), while apparently the details and the results presented in these papers are ignored.

Even the derivation of system (1.2) in [12] is problematic. Starting from the Euler water wave problem, the authors introduce multiple spatial and temporal scales xn=ϵn​xx_{n}=\epsilon^{n}x and tn=ϵn​tt_{n}=\epsilon^{n}t with x0=xx_{0}=x and t0=tt_{0}=t to expand the velocity potential and surface elevation functions in asymptotic series, while assuming that the waves travel in one direction. At the orders ϵ4\epsilon^{4} and ϵ5\epsilon^{5}, the equations of (1.2) arise as a consequence of eliminating secular terms. It is immediately clear that the system (1.2) is troublesome as the two equations appear at different time and spatial scales. This is dealt with in [12] by rewriting the final equations in terms of the first-order slow variables x1x_{1} and t1t_{1}: t2=ϵ​t1t_{2}=\epsilon t_{1}, t3=ϵ2​t1t_{3}=\epsilon^{2}t_{1} and x2=ϵ​x1x_{2}=\epsilon x_{1}, x3=ϵ2​x1x_{3}=\epsilon^{2}x_{1}. Of course this is an inconsistent argument: the different equations encountered to this point are obtained by equating terms at the same order of ϵ\epsilon. Reintroducing ϵ\epsilon at a later point invalidates all calculations to this point. As pointed out in [7], the main problems with the applicability of (1.1) can be summarized as thus:

  • (A)

    Only a system coupling the linear Schrödinger (LS) equation with the KdV equation has ever been derived in (1.2) (see also [9, 11, 13]).

  • (B)

    In the two coupled equations, two different time scales appear.

Moreover, our calculations and results obtained in [7] indicate the impossibility for the derivation of (1.1) in the context of any physical system describing the interaction of long and short waves in dispersive media. It appears impossible even to derive (1.2) with both equations appearing at the same order. But those results are still suggestions nevertheless, as the arguments are based on the fifth-order KdV equation which is just an approximation to the Euler equations. To fully dispute the validity of the system (1.2), one needs to start the analysis from the full Euler equations.

In this manuscript, we will show that in addition to the aforementioned problems A) and B), indeed neither systems (1.1) nor (1.2) can be derived consistently from the full Euler equations formulated in the study of water waves–a confirmation to the suggestions raised earlier in [7].

2 Fundamental equations and summary of results

In this paper, we consider two-dimensional capillary-gravity waves on an inviscid, incompressible fluid layer of uniform depth hh which are governed by the Euler equations

(2.1) ∂2ϕ∂x2+∂2ϕ∂y2=0,x∈ℝ,−1≤y≤η⁡(x,t);\displaystyle\frac{\partial^{2}\phi}{\partial x^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi}{\partial y^{2}}=0,\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\quad-1\leq y\leq\eta(x,t);
(2.2) ∂η∂t−∂ϕ∂y+∂ϕ∂x​∂η∂x=0,at​y=η⁡(x,t);\displaystyle\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial t}-\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial x}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=\eta(x,t);
(2.3) ∂ϕ∂t+12{(∂ϕ∂x)2+(∂ϕ∂y)2}+η−1W∂2η∂x2{1+(∂η∂x)2}−3/2=0,aty=η(x,t);\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial t}+\frac{1}{2}\Big\{(\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x})^{2}+(\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial y})^{2}\Big\}+\eta-\frac{1}{W}\frac{\partial^{2}\eta}{\partial x^{2}}\Big\{1+(\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial x})^{2}\Big\}^{-3/2}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=\eta(x,t);
(2.4) ∂ϕ∂y=0,at​y=−1.\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=-1.

The harmonic function ϕ⁡(x,y,t)\phi(x,y,t) is the velocity potential describing the ir-rotational motion of such fluid for −∞<x<∞-\infty<x<\infty, −1≤y≤η⁡(x,t)-1\leq y\leq\eta(x,t) and tt being the temporal variable. The xx-axis is taken along the undisturbed free surface y=0y=0, the yy-axis is taken vertically upwards, and y=η⁡(x,t)y=\eta(x,t) denotes the elevation of the free surface measured from the undisturbed level. All the quantities have been normalized by the characteristic length hh and the characteristic speed g​h\sqrt{gh}, gg being the gravitational acceleration. The Weber number WW is defined as ρ​g​h2/T\rho gh^{2}/T, where ρ\rho is the fluid density and TT the surface tension. We will make every effort to preserve the usage of notations in [12] as we carry out direct comparisons.

Similar to the approach used in [12], we consider the following asymptotic series

η⁡(x,t,ϵ)=∑n=1∞ϵn​ηn​(x0,x1,x2,⋯,t0,t1,t2,⋯),\eta(x,t;\epsilon)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\epsilon^{n}\eta_{n}(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},\cdots,t_{0},t_{1},t_{2},\cdots),

and

ϕ⁡(x,y,t,ϵ)=∑n=1∞ϵn​ϕn​(x0,x1,x2,⋯,y,t0,t1,t2,⋯),\phi(x,y,t;\epsilon)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\epsilon^{n}\phi_{n}(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},\cdots,y,t_{0},t_{1},t_{2},\cdots),

with

x0=x,t0=t,xn=ϵnx,tn=ϵnt,n=1,2,⋯x_{0}=x,\quad t_{0}=t,\quad x_{n}=\epsilon^{n}x,\quad t_{n}=\epsilon^{n}t,\ n=1,2,\cdots

and expand the equations (2.2), (2.3) around y=0y=0. From these, we obtain a sequence of sets of equations for ηn\eta_{n} and ϕn\phi_{n} from the coefficients of the like powers in ϵ.\epsilon. Notice that in [12], the series expansion for η\eta started at n=2n=2 while that for ϕ\phi started at n=1n=1. This is somewhat awkward even with the physical explanation given in there. Here, we start our expansions for both ϕ\phi and η\eta at the same point n=1n=1 and let the dynamics of the equations (2.1)-(2.4) dictate the relations. It turns out that to have consistency, η1≡0\eta_{1}\equiv 0 and thus all of our calculations agree with those obtained in [12] up to the order ϵ3\epsilon^{3}, except for the presence of the homogeneous solutions which in principle could be omitted, as were taken in [12]. However, at the even orders of ϵ2\epsilon^{2} and ϵ4\epsilon^{4}, the complex amplitudes associated with the non-homogeneous equations arose from (2.1) must vanish due to certain consistency conditions. To be precise, and this is the crux of the matter as to why one can neither derive the system (1.1) nor (1.2), we discuss this point in detail here (see also the equations (3.9), (3.16) and (3.17) below). Let A⁡(x1,t1,…)A(x_{1},t_{1},\ldots) be the complex amplitude representing a train of high frequency short waves, ξ2​(x1,t1,…)\xi_{2}(x_{1},t_{1},\ldots) be a slowly varying low frequency long wave and B⁡(x1,t1,…)B(x_{1},t_{1},\ldots) be the homogeneous solution to the harmonic equation associated with (2.1). At the order ϵ\epsilon, one of the conditions obtained is the dispersion relation

w2=(k+k3W)​tanh⁡k.w^{2}=(k+\frac{k^{3}}{W})\tanh k.

At the order of ϵ2\epsilon^{2}, the corresponding equation for (2.3) reads

F​ei​θ+c.c.+G​e2​θ​i+c.c.+H=0,Fe^{i\theta}+c.c.+Ge^{2\theta i}+c.c.+H=0,

with c.c. signifies the complex conjugate of the previous term and where the functions F,GF,G and HH are given by the following expressions

F={i​w2k−2​i​kW−ik​(1+k2W)​(1+k​cosh⁡k)}​∂A∂x1+{−i​wk​tanh⁡k−iw​(1+k2W)}​∂A∂t1+(1+k2W−w2k​tanh⁡k)​B;\begin{split}F=&\Big\{\frac{iw^{2}}{k}-\frac{2ik}{W}-\frac{i}{k}(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})(1+k\cosh k)\Big\}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}+\Big\{-\frac{iw}{k\tanh k}-\frac{i}{w}(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}\\ &+\big(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W}-\frac{w^{2}}{k\tanh k}\big)B;\end{split}
G={12​(w2tanh2⁡k−w2)+(1+4​k2W)​k2​tanh⁡k}​A2;G=\bigg\{\frac{1}{2}\big(\frac{w^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}-w^{2}\big)+(1+\frac{4k^{2}}{W})\frac{k}{2\tanh k}\bigg\}A^{2};

and

H=∂ψ1∂t1+w2​|A|2tanh2⁡k+w2​|A|2+ξ2.H=\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{w^{2}|A|^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}+w^{2}|A|^{2}+\xi_{2}.

Thus, it must be the case that F=G=H=0F=G=H=0. In particular, the complex amplitude function AA must vanish in order that the dispersion relation mentioned above holds true. The inclusion of homogeneous solutions as mentioned above therefore is necessary. Similar expression appears at the order of ϵ4\epsilon^{4} for the corresponding equation for (2.3). The vanishing condition for GG is in direct contradiction with the dispersion relation unless A≡0A\equiv 0. This is the reason why one cannot derive the couple NLS-KdV system (1.1) from the context of the Euler equations. In principle it could be possible to alter some terms in the Euler equations (2.1)-(2.4) so that second harmonic resonance occurs (that is, the coefficient for GG vanishes) but then we would no longer be dealing with the Euler water wave problem mentioned above.

Starting from the order ϵ4\epsilon^{4}, our results deviate significantly from those obtained in [12]. In particular, the linear Schrödinger equation in the system (1.2), i.e., the first equation, appears at the fifth order instead of fourth in our results. Moreover, at this order ϵ5\epsilon^{5} we also obtain the pure KdV-equation without any coupling term. As none of the calculations were presented after the order of ϵ3\epsilon^{3} in the paper [12], we cannot finger point precisely at what point things start to differ and/or what assumptions had been made to rule out the vanishing of AA in that paper.

Our analysis establishes unequivocally the fact that, contrary to what has been assumed heretofore, one can neither derive the couple linear Schrödinger-KdV system (1.2) nor the NLS-KdV system (1.1) from the Euler equations used in the study of water waves.

3 The main results

3.1 At the order O⁡(ϵ)O(\epsilon)

The first order problem is as follows:

(3.1) ∂2ϕ1∂x02+∂2ϕ1∂y2=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{1}}{\partial y^{2}}=0;
(3.2) ∂η1∂t0−∂ϕ1∂y=0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\eta_{1}}{\partial t_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.3) ∂ϕ1∂t0+η1−1W​∂2η1∂x02=0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial t_{0}}+\eta_{1}-\frac{1}{W}\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{1}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.4) ∂ϕ1∂y=0,at​y=−1.\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=-1.

We take as our starting point the solution for the harmonic function ϕ1\phi_{1} as the superposition of the short and long waves of the following form

(3.5) ϕ1=f⁡(y)​A​(x1,t1,⋯)​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ1​(x1,t1,⋯)\phi_{1}=f(y)A(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots)e^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots)

where θ=k​x0−w​t0\theta=kx_{0}-wt_{0} and A∈ℂ,ψ1∈ℝA\in\mathbb{C},\ \ \psi_{1}\in\mathbb{R} are functions independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y. Substituting (3.5) into (3.1), we have

A⁡[f′′​(y)−k2​f​(y)]​ei​θ+c.c.=0.A[f^{\prime\prime}(y)-k^{2}f(y)]e^{i\theta}+c.c.=0.

Thus, either A=0A=0 or

(3.6) f′′​(y)−k2​f​(y)=0.f^{\prime\prime}(y)-k^{2}f(y)=0.

The ordinary differential equation (3.6) has the solution

f⁡(y)=C1​ek​y+C2​e−k​y,f(y)=C_{1}e^{ky}+C_{2}e^{-ky},

while the boundary condition (3.4) implies that

k​C1​e−k−k​C2​ek=0.kC_{1}e^{-k}-kC_{2}e^{k}=0.

Consequently, it is deduced that

ϕ1=C​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​A​(x1,t1,⋯)​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ1​(x1,t1,⋯).\phi_{1}=C\cosh[k(y+1)]A(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots)e^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots).

Next, it follows from equation (3.2) that

η1=C​k​sinh⁡k−i​w​A​ei​θ+c.c.+ξ1​(x1,t1,⋯)\eta_{1}=\frac{Ck\sinh k}{-iw}Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots)

for some real function ξ1​(x1,t1,⋯).\xi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots). In order to make a direct comparison with the paper [12], we let C=−i​wk​sinh⁡kC=\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k} and obtain

ϕ1=−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​A​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ1​(x1,t1,⋯),\phi_{1}=\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots),

and

(3.7) η1=A​ei​θ+c.c.+ξ1​(x1,t1,⋯).\eta_{1}=Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{1}(x_{1},t_{1},\cdots).

Now, putting the expressions for ϕ1\phi_{1} and η1\eta_{1} obtained above into (3.3), it reveals that

(3.8) −w2​cosh⁡kk​sinh⁡k​A​ei​θ+(1+k2W)​A​ei​θ+c.c.+ξ1=0.\frac{-w^{2}\cosh k}{k\sinh k}Ae^{i\theta}+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{1}=0.

Noting that ξ1\xi_{1} and AA are functions independent of x0,t0x_{0},t_{0}, hence (3.8) implies that

ξ1=0,\xi_{1}=0,

and

A​{−w2​cosh⁡kk​sinh⁡k+(1+k2W)}=0.A\Big\{\frac{-w^{2}\cosh k}{k\sinh k}+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\}=0.

In other words, one has the following dispersion relation

(3.9) w2=(k+k3W)​tanh⁡kw^{2}=(k+\frac{k^{3}}{W})\tanh k

that must hold true unless A=0.A=0. It is therefore concluded that the first order problem in O⁡(ϵ)O(\epsilon) has solution

ϕ1=−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​A​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ1,\phi_{1}=\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{1},

and

η1=A​ei​θ+c.c.,\eta_{1}=Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.,

along with the dispersion relation (3.9), where AA and ψ1\psi_{1} are two arbitrary functions with respect to the variables x1,t1,x2,t2,⋯x_{1},t_{1},x_{2},t_{2},\cdots but independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y.

3.2 At the order O⁡(ϵ2)O(\epsilon^{2})

The second order problem is as follows:

(3.10) ∂2ϕ2∂x02+∂2ϕ2∂y2=−2​∂2ϕ1∂x0​∂x1;\displaystyle\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial y^{2}}=-2\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}};
(3.11) ∂η2∂t0−∂ϕ2∂y=−∂η1∂t1−∂ϕ1∂x0​∂η1∂x0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial t_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial\eta_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{0}}\frac{\partial\eta_{1}}{\partial x_{0}},\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.12) ∂ϕ2∂t0+∂ϕ1∂t1+12​{(∂ϕ1∂x0)2+(∂ϕ1∂y)2}+η2−1W​(∂2η2∂x02+2​∂2η1∂x0​∂x1)=0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial t_{0}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{1}{2}\Big\{(\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{0}})^{2}+(\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial y})^{2}\Big\}+\eta_{2}-\frac{1}{W}(\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+2\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{1}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}})=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.13) ∂ϕ2∂y=0,at​y=−1.\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=-1.

Putting the form of ϕ1\phi_{1} obtained from the order O⁡(ϵ)O(\epsilon) above into (3.10) we have

∂2ϕ2∂x02+∂2ϕ2∂y2=−2​wsinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+c.c.,\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial y^{2}}=-\frac{2w}{\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.,

which has solution

(3.14) ϕ2=−w⁡(y+1)k​sinh⁡k​sinh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​B​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ2,\phi_{2}=-\frac{w(y+1)}{k\sinh k}\sinh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]Be^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{2},

where BB and ψ2\psi_{2} are arbitrary functions independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y. Next, it follows from (3.11) that

∂η2∂t0=∂ϕ2∂y−∂A∂t1​ei​θ−i​k​wtanh⁡k​A2​e2​θ​i+c.c.=−wk​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ−i​w​B​ei​θ−∂A∂t1​ei​θ−i​k​wtanh⁡k​A2​e2​θ​i+c.c..\begin{split}\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial t_{0}}&=\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{ikw}{\tanh k}A^{2}e^{2\theta i}+c.c.\\ &=-\frac{w}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}-iwBe^{i\theta}-\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{ikw}{\tanh k}A^{2}e^{2\theta i}+c.c..\end{split}

Integrating the above equation with respect to t0t_{0} we obtain

(3.15) η2=−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+B​ei​θ−iw​∂A∂t1​ei​θ+k2​tanh⁡k​A2​e2​θ​i+c.c.+ξ2,\eta_{2}=-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+Be^{i\theta}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{k}{2\tanh k}A^{2}e^{2\theta i}+c.c.+\xi_{2},

where ξ2\xi_{2} is an arbitrary function independent of the slow variables x0,t0,y.x_{0},t_{0},y. Substituting (3.14) and (3.15) into (3.12), we deduce that

i​w2k​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+−w2k​tanh⁡k​B​ei​θ+−i​wk​tanh⁡k​∂A∂t1​ei​θ+∂ψ1∂t1+12​{w2​A2tanh2⁡k​e2​θ​i+2​w2​|A|2tanh2⁡k−w2​A2​e2​θ​i+2​w2​|A|2}+(1+k2W)​{−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+B​ei​θ−iw​∂A∂t1​ei​θ}+(1+4​k2W)​k2​tanh⁡k​A2​e2​θ​i+ξ2−2​i​kW​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+c.c.=0.\begin{split}&\frac{iw^{2}}{k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{-w^{2}}{k\tanh k}Be^{i\theta}+\frac{-iw}{k\tanh k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}\\ &+\frac{1}{2}\Big\{\frac{w^{2}A^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}e^{2\theta i}+2\frac{w^{2}|A|^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}-w^{2}A^{2}e^{2\theta i}+2w^{2}|A|^{2}\Big\}\\ &+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+Be^{i\theta}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}\Big\}\\ &+(1+\frac{4k^{2}}{W})\frac{k}{2\tanh k}A^{2}e^{2\theta i}+\xi_{2}-\frac{2ik}{W}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.=0.\\ \end{split}

The above equation can be rewritten in the following compact form

(3.16) F​ei​θ+G​e2​θ​i+c.c.+H=0,Fe^{i\theta}+Ge^{2\theta i}+c.c.+H=0,

where the functions F,GF,G and HH are given by the following expressions

F=i​w2k​∂A∂x1+−i​wk​tanh⁡k​∂A∂t1+(1+k2W)​{−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1−iw​∂A∂t1}−2​i​kW​∂A∂x1+−w2k​tanh⁡k​B+(1+k2W)​B;\begin{split}F&=\frac{iw^{2}}{k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}+\frac{-iw}{k\tanh k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}\Big\}\\ &\quad-\frac{2ik}{W}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}+\frac{-w^{2}}{k\tanh k}B+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})B;\end{split}
G=12​{w2​A2tanh2⁡k−w2​A2}+(1+4​k2W)​k2​tanh⁡k​A2;G=\frac{1}{2}\Big\{\frac{w^{2}A^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}-w^{2}A^{2}\Big\}+(1+\frac{4k^{2}}{W})\frac{k}{2\tanh k}A^{2};

and

H=∂ψ1∂t1+w2​|A|2tanh2⁡k+w2​|A|2+ξ2.H=\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{w^{2}|A|^{2}}{\tanh^{2}k}+w^{2}|A|^{2}+\xi_{2}.

Thus, (3.16) implies that

(3.17) F=G=H=0.F=G=H=0.

In particular, G=0G=0 implies that A=0A=0, otherwise a contradiction to the dispersion relation (3.8) will arise. Thus, (3.17) reduces to the condition

(3.18) ∂ψ1∂t1+ξ2=0,\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}}+\xi_{2}=0,

apart from (3.9). We therefore conclude that

η1=0,ϕ1=ψ1,\eta_{1}=0,\ \ \phi_{1}=\psi_{1},
(3.19) ϕ2=−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​A​ei​θ+c.c.+ψ2,\phi_{2}=\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\psi_{2},

and

(3.20) η2=A​ei​θ+c.c.+ξ2,\eta_{2}=Ae^{i\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{2},

where, in the interest of preserving the same notations as in [12] for direct comparison, we have renamed BB by A.A.

Remark 1. The second term with the function BB in the right hand side of (3.14), which represents the homogeneous solution, was omitted in [12]. It is now clear that its inclusion is necessary. Notice that in [12] the asymptotic expansion for ϕ\phi started at n=1n=1 while that for η\eta started at n=2n=2. This is somewhat awkward. Here, we start both of the expansions at the same point n=1n=1 and let the dynamics of the problem dictate the relation. In order to have consistency, η1\eta_{1} must vanish and we arrive at the exact same results as obtained in [12].

3.3 At the third order in O⁡(ϵ3)O(\epsilon^{3})

The third order problem is as follows:

(3.21) ∂2ϕ3∂x02+∂2ϕ3∂y2=−2​∂2ϕ2∂x0​∂x1−∂2ϕ1∂2x1;\displaystyle\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{3}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{3}}{\partial y^{2}}=-2\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}}-\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{1}}{\partial^{2}x_{1}};
(3.22) ∂η3∂t0−∂ϕ3∂y=−∂η2∂t1,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\eta_{3}}{\partial t_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{3}}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial t_{1}},\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.23) ∂ϕ3∂t0+∂ϕ2∂t1+∂ϕ1∂t2+η3−1W​(∂2η3∂x02+2​∂2η2∂x0​∂x1)=0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{3}}{\partial t_{0}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial t_{2}}+\eta_{3}-\frac{1}{W}(\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{3}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+2\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}})=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.24) ∂ϕ3∂y=0,at​y=−1.\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{3}}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=-1.

Introducing the form of ϕ2\phi_{2} obtained from (3.19) into (3.21), we have

∂2ϕ3∂x02+∂2ϕ3∂y2=−2​wsinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+c.c−∂2ψ1∂x12.\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{3}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{3}}{\partial y^{2}}=-\frac{2w}{\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}.

This has a solution given by the following form

(3.25) ϕ3=−w⁡(y+1)k​sinh⁡k​sinh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​B​ei​θ+c.c.−12​∂2ψ1∂x12​(y+1)2+ψ3,\phi_{3}=-\frac{w(y+1)}{k\sinh k}\sinh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]Be^{i\theta}+c.c.-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}(y+1)^{2}+\psi_{3},

where B∈ℂB\in\mathbb{C} (the homogeneous solution) and ψ3∈ℝ\psi_{3}\in\mathbb{R} are arbitrary functions independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y. Next, it follows from (3.22) that

∂η3∂t0=∂ϕ3∂y−∂A∂t1​ei​θ+c.c.−∂ξ2∂t1=−wk​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ−i​w​B​ei​θ−∂2ψ1∂x12−∂A∂t1​ei​θ+c.c.−∂ξ2∂t1.\begin{split}\frac{\partial\eta_{3}}{\partial t_{0}}&=\frac{\partial\phi_{3}}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.-\frac{\partial\xi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}\\ &=-\frac{w}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}-iwBe^{i\theta}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}-\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.-\frac{\partial\xi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}.\end{split}

Integrating the above equation with respect to t0t_{0} we obtain

(3.26) η3=−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+B​ei​θ−iw​∂A∂t1​ei​θ+c.c.+ξ3,\eta_{3}=-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+Be^{i\theta}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{3},

where ξ3∈ℝ\xi_{3}\in\mathbb{R} is an arbitrary function independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y, provided that the non-secularity condition

(3.27) ∂ξ2∂t1+∂2ψ1∂x12=0\frac{\partial\xi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}=0

is satisfied. Substituting (3.25) and (3.26) into (3.23), we arrive at

i​w2k​∂A∂x1​ei​θ−w2k​tanh⁡k​B​ei​θ−i​wk​tanh⁡k​∂A∂t1​ei​θ+∂ψ2∂t1+∂ψ1∂t2+(1+k2W)​{−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+B​ei​θ−iw​∂A∂t1​ei​θ}+ξ3−2​i​kW​∂A∂x1​ei​θ+c.c.=0.\begin{split}&\frac{iw^{2}}{k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{w^{2}}{k\tanh k}Be^{i\theta}-\frac{iw}{k\tanh k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{\partial\psi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{2}}\\ &+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+Be^{i\theta}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}\Big\}\\ &+\xi_{3}-\frac{2ik}{W}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.=0.\\ \end{split}

From this, one can see that

(3.28) i​w2k​∂A∂x1−i​wk​tanh⁡k​∂A∂t1+(1+k2W)​{−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂A∂x1−iw​∂A∂t1}−2​i​kW​∂A∂x1=0,\frac{iw^{2}}{k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}-\frac{iw}{k\tanh k}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}+(1+\frac{k^{2}}{W})\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}\Big\}-\frac{2ik}{W}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}=0,

and

(3.29) ∂ψ2∂t1+∂ψ1∂t2+ξ3=0,\frac{\partial\psi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{2}}+\xi_{3}=0,

as the coefficient for BB happens to satisfy the dispersive relation (3.9).

The equation (3.28) can be rewritten as

(3.30) ∂A∂t1+Vg​∂A∂x1=0,\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{1}}+V_{g}\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{1}}=0,

where VgV_{g} denotes the group velocity

(3.31) Vg=d​wd​k=12​w​[(1+3​k2W)​tanh⁡k+(k+k3W)​sech2​k].V_{g}=\frac{dw}{dk}=\frac{1}{2w}\Big[(1+\frac{3k^{2}}{W})\tanh k+(k+\frac{k^{3}}{W}){\rm sech}^{2}k\Big].

Eliminating of ξ2\xi_{2} between (3.18) and (3.27) yields

(3.32) ∂2ψ1∂t12−∂2ψ1∂x12=0.\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}^{2}}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}=0.

Remark 2. Thus, up to the order of O⁡(ϵ3)O(\epsilon^{3}), all of our analysis reveals exact same results as those obtained in [12]. Starting from the next order, however, the analysis will differ significantly.

3.4 At the fourth order in O⁡(ϵ4)O(\epsilon^{4})

The fourth order problem is as follows:

(3.33) ∂2ϕ4∂x02+∂2ϕ4∂y2=−2​∂2ϕ3∂x0​∂x1−2​∂2ϕ2∂x0​∂x2−∂2ϕ2∂x12−2​∂2ϕ1∂x1​∂x2;\displaystyle\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{4}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{4}}{\partial y^{2}}=-2\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{3}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}}-2\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{2}}-\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}-2\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}};
(3.34) ∂η4∂t0−∂ϕ4∂y=−∂η3∂t1−∂η2∂t2−∂ϕ1∂x1​∂η2∂x0−∂ϕ2∂x0​∂η2∂x0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\frac{\partial\eta_{4}}{\partial t_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{4}}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial\eta_{3}}{\partial t_{1}}-\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial t_{2}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}}\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}}\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}},\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
∂ϕ4∂t0+∂ϕ3∂t1+∂ϕ2∂t2+∂ϕ1∂t3+12​{(∂ϕ1∂x1+∂ϕ2∂x0)2+(∂ϕ2∂y)2}\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{4}}{\partial t_{0}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{3}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial t_{2}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial t_{3}}+\frac{1}{2}\Big\{(\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}}+\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}})^{2}+(\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial y})^{2}\Big\}
(3.35) +η4−1W​(∂2η4∂x02+2​∂2η3∂x0​∂x1+2​∂2η2∂x0​∂x2+∂2η2∂x12)=0,at​y=0;\displaystyle\quad+\eta_{4}-\frac{1}{W}(\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{4}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+2\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{3}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{1}}+2\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}\partial x_{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}})=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=0;
(3.36) ∂ϕ4∂y=0,at​y=−1.\displaystyle\frac{\partial\phi_{4}}{\partial y}=0,\quad\text{at}\ y=-1.

Introducing (3.19) and (3.25) into (3.33), we have

∂2ϕ4∂x02+∂2ϕ4∂y2=2​i​w​(y+1)sinh⁡k​sinh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂2A∂x12​ei​θ−2​wsinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂B∂x1​ei​θ−2​wsinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x2​ei​θ+i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂2A∂x12​ei​θ+c.c.−∂2ψ2∂x12−2​∂2ψ1∂x1​∂x2.\begin{split}\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{4}}{\partial x_{0}^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2}\phi_{4}}{\partial y^{2}}&=\frac{2iw(y+1)}{\sinh k}\sinh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{2w}{\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial B}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}\\ &-\frac{2w}{\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}+c.c.-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}-2\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}}.\\ \end{split}

This equation has a solution given by the following form

(3.37) ϕ4=−w⁡(y+1)k​sinh⁡k​sinh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂A∂x2​ei​θ+i​w​(y+1)22​k​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂2A∂x12​ei​θ−w⁡(y+1)k​sinh⁡k​sinh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​∂B∂x1​ei​θ+−i​wk​sinh⁡k​cosh⁡[k⁡(y+1)]​B~​ei​θ+c.c.−12​∂2ψ2∂x12​(y+1)2−∂2ψ1∂x1​∂x2​(y+1)2+ψ4,\begin{split}\phi_{4}&=-\frac{w(y+1)}{k\sinh k}\sinh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{iw(y+1)^{2}}{2k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}\\ &-\frac{w(y+1)}{k\sinh k}\sinh[k(y+1)]\frac{\partial B}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{-iw}{k\sinh k}\cosh[k(y+1)]\widetilde{B}e^{i\theta}+c.c.\\ &-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}(y+1)^{2}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}}(y+1)^{2}+\psi_{4},\\ \end{split}

where B~∈ℂ\widetilde{B}\in\mathbb{C} (the homogeneous solution) and ψ4∈ℝ\psi_{4}\in\mathbb{R} are arbitrary functions independent of the slow variables x0,t0,yx_{0},t_{0},y. Next, by putting the expressions previously obtained for ϕ4,η3,η2\phi_{4},\eta_{3},\eta_{2} into (3.34), we have

∂η4∂t0=∂ϕ4∂y−∂η3∂t1−∂η2∂t2−∂ϕ1∂x1​∂η2∂x0−∂ϕ2∂x0​∂η2∂x0={−wk(1+kcothk)∂A∂x2ei​θ+i​w2​k(k+2cothk)∂2A∂x12ei​θ−wk(1+kcothk)∂B∂x1ei​θ−iwB~ei​θ−∂2ψ2∂x12−2∂2ψ1∂x1​∂x2}−{−ik​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂2A∂x1​∂t1​ei​θ+∂B∂t1​ei​θ−iw​∂2A∂t12​ei​θ+∂ξ3∂t1}−{∂A∂t2​ei​θ+∂ξ2∂t2}−i​k​∂ϕ1∂x1​A​ei​θ−i​k​wtanh⁡k​A2​ei​2​θ+c.c..\begin{split}\frac{\partial\eta_{4}}{\partial t_{0}}&=\frac{\partial\phi_{4}}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial\eta_{3}}{\partial t_{1}}-\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial t_{2}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}}\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}}-\frac{\partial\phi_{2}}{\partial x_{0}}\frac{\partial\eta_{2}}{\partial x_{0}}\\ &=\Big\{-\frac{w}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{iw}{2k}(k+2\coth k)\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}\\ &\quad-\frac{w}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial B}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}-iw\widetilde{B}e^{i\theta}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}-2\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}}\Big\}\\ &-\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{\partial B}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial t_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{\partial\xi_{3}}{\partial t_{1}}\Big\}\\ &-\Big\{\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{\partial\xi_{2}}{\partial t_{2}}\Big\}-ik\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}}Ae^{i\theta}-\frac{ikw}{\tanh k}A^{2}e^{i2\theta}+c.c..\\ \end{split}

An integration with respect to the slow variable t0t_{0} gives

η4={−ik(1+kcothk)∂A∂x2ei​θ−12​k(k+2cothk)∂2A∂x12ei​θ−ik(1+kcothk)∂B∂x1ei​θ+B~ei​θ}−{1w​k​(1+k​coth⁡k)​∂2A∂x1​∂t1​ei​θ+iw​∂B∂t1​ei​θ+1w2​∂2A∂t12​ei​θ}−iw​∂A∂t2​ei​θ+kw​∂ϕ1∂x1​A​ei​θ+k2​tanh⁡k​A2​ei​2​θ+c.c.+ξ4,\begin{split}\eta_{4}&=\Big\{-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_{2}}e^{i\theta}-\frac{1}{2k}(k+2\coth k)\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}\\ &\quad-\frac{i}{k}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial B}{\partial x_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\widetilde{B}e^{i\theta}\Big\}\\ &-\Big\{\frac{1}{wk}(1+k\coth k)\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial x_{1}\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial B}{\partial t_{1}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{1}{w^{2}}\frac{\partial^{2}A}{\partial t_{1}^{2}}e^{i\theta}\Big\}\\ &-\frac{i}{w}\frac{\partial A}{\partial t_{2}}e^{i\theta}+\frac{k}{w}\frac{\partial\phi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}}Ae^{i\theta}+\frac{k}{2\tanh k}A^{2}e^{i2\theta}+c.c.+\xi_{4},\\ \end{split}

provided that the non-secularity condition

(3.38) ∂2ψ2∂x12+2​∂2ψ1∂x1​∂x2+∂ξ3∂t1+∂ξ2∂t2=0\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}+2\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}}+\frac{\partial\xi_{3}}{\partial t_{1}}+\frac{\partial\xi_{2}}{\partial t_{2}}=0

holds true. Eliminating of ξ2,ξ3\xi_{2},\xi_{3} between (3.18), (3.29) and (3.38) yields

∂2ψ2∂t12−∂2ψ2∂x12+2​(∂2ψ1∂t1​∂t2−∂2ψ1∂x1​∂x2)=0.\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial t_{1}^{2}}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{2}}{\partial x_{1}^{2}}+2(\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial t_{1}\partial t_{2}}-\frac{\partial^{2}\psi_{1}}{\partial x_{1}\partial x_{2}})=0.

Remark 3. Because of the vanishing condition (3.39) on AA, the linear Schrödinger equation ( i.e. the first equation in (1.2)) does not appear in our analysis at this order of ϵ4\epsilon^{4} as in [12]. Since none of the calculations were presented after the order of ϵ3\epsilon^{3} in the paper [12], we cannot finger point precisely at what point things start to differ and/or what assumptions had been made to rule out the vanishing of AA in that paper.

The equation (3.49) is the linear Schrödinger equation.

Remark 4. It is therefore established that both the linear Schrödinger (3.49) and KdV (3.46) equations appear at the same order O⁡(ϵ5)O(\epsilon^{5}). However, there is no coupling terms in the KdV equation.
